summary: Dependency-confusion beacon in @myorder-frontend-commons/analytics exfiltrates host identity on install
details: The package ships an inert index.js that exports empty analytics stubs, while package.json wires all three lifecycle hooks (preinstall, install, postinstall) to execute poc.js. On every install poc.js collects host identifiers (hostname, username, platform/arch/release, cwd, Node version, CI environment variable presence) and sends them via HTTP GET to a hardcoded out-of-band callback at an oast.fun Interactsh subdomain, with a backup to an nip.io IP-encoded host (80-190-83-27.nip.io). The scoped name @myorder-frontend-commons/analytics combined with the implausibly high version 101.0.0 and the absence of any real functionality matches the dependency-confusion attack shape: a public package published to shadow an internal name so that resolution pulls the attacker's code into private build environments. A self-description as an authorized proof-of-concept does not change the behavior: installers do not consent, and the destinations are external OOB infrastructure, not installer-controlled.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
